hypothesis: Selection union/subtraction combine relative and absolute storage without normalizing coordinate frames.
supportedSetup: Production terrain creates one ROOM at relative (10,10), absolute (11,10), in default frame xstart=1. Exported selection_area and selection_match constructors both semantically select that cell. Each operand is independently consumed by production terrain and asserted to paint only (11,10). Production l_selection_or/sub then combine them and terrain consumes the result. No coordinate-marker mutations or injected loaders.
contractRationale: C area translates coordinates before storing; C match stores map coordinates. C public union/subtraction accept arbitrary selections without a constructor-origin restriction. The JS constructors return supported ThemeroomSelection operands and each independently denotes the same map cell. Mixing these exported API results is valid composition, not a fabricated inconsistent state.
expectedC: Union of identical singleton selections paints only (11,10); subtraction is empty in both operand orders.
observedJS: Relative/absolute union paints (11,10) and (12,10); reversed order paints (10,10) and (11,10). Subtraction retains (11,10) in both orders.
control: Relative/relative and absolute/absolute controls match for union and subtraction, four controls total. Independent operand-consumer checks all match the same singleton.
semanticCause: One coordinate-frame normalization defect, with union and subtraction manifestations.
scope: Eight finite compositions; supported API parity only. Shipped mixed-constructor exposure and hidden-score impact unknown. Same-frame numeric semantics and unrelated operators are not implicated.
oracleProvenance: Exact l_selection_or/sub function bodies executed with fixed argument adapter and minimal integer point storage/bounds. C operands are the valid singleton postconditions of area and match, supported by wrapper-source contract and independently verified JS API consumption. Full Lua parser and C constructor execution are not claimed. Adapter only passes two selections and retrieves result, not an arbitrary Lua runtime.
